series.why_a_new_name: data/progression.json's series/active key (kanto, johto, ...) is the campaign's REGION; this is rctmod's per-player series. A Challenge player is in rctmod series cobblers_challenge and campaign region kanto at once (RCT_PER_PLAYER_MODE.md section 4).
series.title: Kanto: Full-Team rules
series.description: Every Gym Leader brings six. The level limits are the ones the Standard rules use.
series.difficulty_why: rctmod's series metadata is a 1..10 number on the trainer card. Kanto's own file says 7 (COBBLEVERSE-RCT-DP-v20 data/rctmod/series/kanto.json). Kept equal: the owner asked for the two modes to be told apart by what they mean for the journey, never as easier and harder, and a bigger number on the card would say exactly that.
series.caps_why: No initialLevelCap or relativeLevelCap: the config's 20 and 0 apply, as for Kanto, so a Challenge player's cap follows the same curve (RCT_PER_PLAYER_MODE.md section 3, condition 3). Every Challenge boss team tops out at its record's ace_level (docs/story/generate_trainers.py build_boss_mode refuses otherwise), so no per-trainer relativeLevelCap is needed; tools/challenge_mode.py asserts it.

mode.tag_why: A scoreboard tag on the player, set in the same action that runs the series command, so a selector (the route trainers' swap, tools/route_trainers.py) can tell a Challenge player apart without reading player data. The lock field stays the truth for the dialogue.

bosses_why: The thirteen Kanto series trainers: the eight leaders (data/gym_trainers.json) and the Elite Four and Champion (data/league_trainers.json), each an upstream id our team overrides. Each gets a SECOND id <upstream>_challenge carrying its record's Challenge team. upstream_mob is what tools/challenge_mode.py writes for the new id besides series and requiredDefeats; it is the upstream mob file's other fields, READ from COBBLEVERSE-RCT-DP-v20.zip data/rctmod/mobs/trainers/single/<upstream>.json on 2026-10-06 (local snapshot C:/Users/wnd/Documents/cobblers-local/server-snapshot-2026-10-05/datapacks). requiredDefeats is that file's chain with every id suffixed. advancement is upstream's own defeat advancement in COBBLEVERSE-DP-v31 (data/cobbleverse/advancement/trainer/kanto/), granted to a Challenge winner so everything that keys on it -- the League's elevator (data/structures.json kanto_league required_advancements: defeat_elite_lance), the League hold-off in tools/route_trainers.py, the Champion's door -- works for both modes. lang is the prefix of upstream's translatable battle lines (dialogs.rctmod.<lang>.<context>.<n>), read from the same zip; the Elite Four and Champion use our own lines from data/league_trainers.json instead.

upstream_battle_line_counts.why: How many translatable variants each upstream LEADER dialog file carries per battle context (all eight identical), read from COBBLEVERSE-RCT-DP-v20.zip data/rctmod/dialogs/trainers/single/kanto_<leader>.json on 2026-10-06. A Challenge leader speaks the same person's lines: no Codex text exists for the leaders yet (tools/route_trainers.py: 'their dialogue is Codex's to write').

routes_why: Route trainers (Routes 1-8 and Victory Road's ten, every record with modes.challenge whose seat tools/route_trainers.py places) get <id>_challenge too, but NOT a second entity: one trainer stands at each seat, and the trainers cycle swaps its TrainerId to the Challenge id while the nearest player within its reach carries the mode tag, and back otherwise, never during a battle (RCT_PER_PLAYER_MODE.md section 5 option R-b). That swap is ASSUMED to work (experiment E7 in that document): a data merge of TrainerId reloads the entity through readAdditionalSaveData -> setTrainerId, which was read from source, not run. If it does not work, a Challenge player meets the Normal team on routes; nothing else breaks. The Normal ids stay seriesless as before; each Challenge id is in series cobblers_challenge, optional, with no requiredDefeats, so neither moves a level cap (section 3). The mansion guardians, the HQ tower's seven and the arena's records carry no modes and get no Challenge id.
owner_decision: DECIDED by the owner on 2026-10-07 (docs/STATE.md 'What is decided', the owner's answers item 6; docs/HANDOVER_SESSION.md section 2b item 6): ONE leader per gym. All thirteen bosses stand as one person: the Normal spawner stays, the second (Challenge) spawner goes, and the trainers cycle swaps the spawner's TrainerIds and the standing trainer's TrainerId to <id>_challenge while the nearest player within reach carries the mode tag, back otherwise, never during a battle. Order: proven on Brock in staging first, then the other twelve, by widening single_leader.rollout. Until a boss is in the rollout it keeps the earlier build: both leaders, the Challenge one on bosses[].spawner.at.

single_leader.rollout_why: A list of bosses ids, or "all". Brock only until the staging proof in docs/mechanics/ONE_LEADER_SWAP.md passes (the owner's order). A boss here gets no place_<id>_challenge function and no place line; the cycle's swap drives its one spawner (data/gym_buildings leader.spawner, data/gym_interiors.json expect_spawner_at, or single_leader.normal_at for the League, which no other record carries), and reapply step R17L runs cobblers:trainers/challenge/retire_<id>_challenge once to remove the second spawner a world already holds at bosses[].spawner.at, which therefore stays recorded. A template boss (Misty, the League) also needs single_leader.restore {floor, under}: what its second spawner and redstone block replaced, measured from the template; a gym_buildings boss reads them from its own gym model.
single_leader.reach_why: rctmod-server.toml forceBattleMaxDistance (16.0) + 1, computed by tools/challenge_mode.py reach(): the farthest a trainer starts a battle on sight, so within it the leader already carries the nearest player's mode, and beyond it no battle can start.
